briefdescription.para: A REPLACE/DELETE request is supposed to delete the old tuple from all indexes.

detaileddescription.para: In order to generate a DELETE statement for a secondary index, we need to look up the old tuple in the primary index, which is expensive as it implies a random disk access. We can optimize out the lookup by deferring generation of the DELETE statement until primary index compaction.

The following flag is set for those REPLACE and DELETE statements that skipped deletion of the old tuple from secondary indexes. It makes the write iterator generate DELETE statements for them during compaction.

briefdescription.para: Statements that have this flag set are ignored by the read iterator.

detaileddescription.para: We set this flag for deferred DELETE statements, because they may violate the invariant which the read relies upon: the older a source, the older statements it stores for a particular key.

briefdescription.para: This flag is set for those REPLACE statements that were generated by UPDATE operations.

detaileddescription.para: It is used by the write iterator to turn such REPLACEs into INSERTs in secondary indexes so that they can get annihilated with DELETEs on compaction. It is never written to disk.
